Problem: low bids that lead to poor quality or surprise costs

Ultra-low bids often mean cheap materials, uninsured labor, or missing line items. A bid that doesn't include plywood replacement, disposal fees, or permit costs will result in surprise charges once work begins.

items.v: Insist on detailed written estimates that specify every cost and material
Ask specifically about decking replacement rates, debris disposal, and permit handling

Problem: contractors who disappear or delay work
Some contractors take a deposit then stall, or don't return to finish the punch list. This is especially common with storm chasers who move from area to area.

items.v: Check the company's presence and verify they have a real, established base in the Newark area
Confirm years in business locally-stable, long-running local operation is the kind of track record you want to see
Structure payments with reasonable deposits (not full prepayment) and tie payments to completed milestones
Ensure the contract includes written change-order procedures and completion dates

runs.v: Problem: code violations and failed inspections

Common code issues in Newark include improper roof overlays (layering new shingles over old without tear-off when code requires it), inadequate ventilation, and incorrect flashing on flat roofs. Under Newark's building ordinances, failures to comply with permit and code requirements can result in stop-work orders, fines, and invalidation of insurance claims.

For homes that are detached one- or two-family dwellings, simple replacement of roofing covering without affecting structure is often classified as ordinary maintenance and does not require a permit. Verbal promises, unclear workmanship warranty length, and missing manufacturer registration leave homeowners unprotected. Warranties should last at least 5 to 10 years for workmanship-anything less raises a red flag.
